original_question: A 6-year-old male who recently immigrated to the United States from Asia is admitted to the hospital with dyspnea. Physical exam reveals a gray pseudomembrane in the patient's oropharynx along with lymphadenopathy. The patient develops myocarditis and expires on hospital day 5. Which of the following would have prevented this patient's presentation and decline?

base.stage_1: A 6-year-old male, recent immigrant from Asia, presents to the emergency department with dyspnea.
base.stage_2: On physical examination, a gray pseudomembrane is noted in the patient's oropharynx. Cervical lymphadenopathy is also present. Vital signs show elevated heart rate and respiratory rate.
base.stage_3: Laboratory studies reveal elevated inflammatory markers. An EKG shows evidence of myocarditis. Chest X-ray is unremarkable.
base.stage_4: Culture of the oropharyngeal membrane grows Corynebacterium diphtheriae. Toxin assay is positive for diphtheria toxin.

counterfactuals.alteration_description: The absence of a pseudomembrane in the oropharynx makes diphtheria much less likely.
counterfactuals.stage_1: A 6-year-old male, recent immigrant from Asia, presents to the emergency department with dyspnea.
counterfactuals.stage_2: On physical examination, the oropharynx appears normal without any pseudomembrane. Cervical lymphadenopathy is also present. Vital signs show elevated heart rate and respiratory rate.
counterfactuals.stage_3: Laboratory studies reveal elevated inflammatory markers. An EKG shows evidence of myocarditis. Chest X-ray is unremarkable.
counterfactuals.stage_4: Culture of the oropharyngeal membrane grows Corynebacterium diphtheriae. Toxin assay is positive for diphtheria toxin.
